content.text:
I'm trying to locate the center of symmetry in this 10-row, 9-column grid of 8s, guessing it's around row 5, col 4, and working out the rotation formula that maps points clockwise around that center.

Testing several cells against center (5,4), some rotations line up perfectly with 8s while others don't, so I try (4,4) as an alternative center but that also fails on some cells. I'm now cataloging every nonzero cell in the grid by row to systematically check which center actually satisfies all the rotational mappings.

Checking the remaining rotation candidates confirms none besides (2,4) with color 4 work out, since all other transformed positions land on existing 8s. So the answer is: (2,4) becomes 0, and the 4 gets placed at (4,7).

I'm guessing the center is around (4,7) and looking for the rarest colors to identify the odd cell, checking whether a 90-degree rotation around that center maps certain cells to zero.

Testing each candidate, 6, 1, and 5 all rotate onto non-zero cells and fail, but the 7 at (2,8) rotates onto a zero at (5,9), making it the standout match at distance 3 from center. That seems like the winning candidate, so I'll go with 7 moving to (5,9), assuming the center guess of (4,7) holds.
